page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-focused instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The instance provisions 8 vCPUs across 4 physical dedicated cores with two threads per core. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory is fixed at 16.0 GB, establishing a lean 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server includes no GPUs and no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached persistent disks for file systems.

Instruction set support features advanced vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512, AMX-tile, AMX-INT8, and AVX-VNNI, alongside cryptographic hardware acceleration including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. Synthetic benchmarks reflect solid single-thread performance, with the Geekbench single-core score reaching 2317.0 and text processing measuring 3051.0, both placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression at 35.04 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.86 GB/sec also display strong results.

Multi-core execution aligns with standard middle-tier performance profiles, showing a Geekbench multi-core score of 8819.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 12271.85. Memory subsystem throughput reaches 70.65 GB/sec for uncached read-only workloads and 40.19 GB/sec for uncached write operations. In workload-specific tests, the instance supports 12.43 million Redis SET operations per second and 17.08 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based inference shows limitations on larger language models, falling into the bottom 25% with 8.54 tokens/sec on text generation for 7B parameter models.

Given its 2 GB per core ratio, the instance yields high compute efficiency for CPU-bound pipelines without the cost overhead of unutilized system memory. It is appropriate for single-threaded or CPU-intensive tasks, CI/CD compilation runs, web serving, and lightweight caching layers, while remaining constrained for in-memory databases or large memory workloads due to its 16 GB boundary.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with 8 vCPUs (4 dedicated physical cores) clocked at 2.3 GHz and 16.0 GB of memory. Designed with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, it lacks local storage and bundled GPUs, relying on external network storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier single-core performance, recording 2317.0 in Geekbench single-core and 35.04 GB/sec in gzip compression, alongside robust support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Multi-threaded and memory bandwidth metrics place comfortably within the median range, delivering 12.43 million Redis SET operations per second and 17.08 GB/sec of static web throughput. Due to its lean 16 GB allocation, the server offers efficient compute density for CPU-heavy tasks, code compilation, build pipelines, and front-end web serving, while being unsuited for memory-heavy databases or large model inference.
